Comparing Ukraine to Israel — and then saying Ukraine no longer deserves support — is a serious stretch.
Ukraine was invaded. Iran has supplied Shahed drones that have been used extensively against Ukrainian cities and civilians. Treating the disruption of that supply relationship as the moment Ukraine becomes the villain is backwards.
Ukraine is a sovereign country. If it wants to pursue NATO membership, that is its decision. Russia does not get a veto over another country’s alliances. Framing NATO discussion as the main “provocation” while soft-pedaling a full-scale invasion is a familiar talking point, not a serious account of who started the war.
You’ve defended armed resistance when it’s directed at Israel as justified self-defense. Yet when Ukraine acts against a supplier of weapons already being used to kill its civilians, suddenly it’s “becoming Israel” and no longer deserves support. That is not a consistent standard on civilian lives or the right to defend against ongoing attacks.
If civilian deaths matter, they matter when Russia does it too. Withdrawing support over this effectively treats continued Russian strikes on Ukrainian civilians as the lesser issue. That is selective, not principled.
The point is that Ukraine disrupting a weapons supply used against its own population is not the same thing, and treating it as the disqualifying act is a double standard.
